Campaign brief: Resend gives this engineer a documented path to route Supabase Auth email through a dedicated sending provider with explicit plan limits, while leaving control of Supabase’s separate Auth rate limit in their hands.
events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
events.reader_segment: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does
events.promise: Resend gives this engineer a documented path to route Supabase Auth email through a dedicated sending provider with explicit plan limits, while leaving control of Supabase’s separate Auth rate limit in their hands.
events.arc: In one email, move the reader from recognizing the built-in Auth sender as a launch constraint to seeing a concrete, bounded migration path they can inspect before changing production.

emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the Supabase-specific SMTP setup and decide whether Resend is the right sending provider for authentication email before their next launch or traffic increase.
emails.single_idea: Resend is available as a custom SMTP provider for Supabase Auth: connect it with Resend credentials, then set Supabase’s separate Auth rate limit deliberately. Resend Pro removes Resend’s daily sending cap; the Free plan remains limited to 100 emails per day.
emails.objection: Changing the sender for authentication email sounds like a project with another set of limits to discover.
must_not_say: Do not claim Resend changes, bypasses, or automatically raises Supabase’s Auth rate limit.
Do not claim Resend detects or survives Supabase dashboard actions that erase SMTP settings.
Do not explain or promise to fix how Supabase counts messages against its own limit.
Do not imply the Resend Free plan removes daily caps; it is limited to 100 emails per day and 3,000 per month.
Do not promise uninterrupted authentication email, guaranteed inbox placement, or a full migration time.
Do not claim transactional and marketing sending are isolated by account or infrastructure; dedicated-IP isolation is outside this email’s argument.
Do not add Broadcasts, Automations, Templates, dedicated IPs, security certifications, customer-logo lists, or broad SDK coverage.
Do not describe Resend as faster, broader, higher quality, easier, more controllable, or more secure than competitors.
Do not state or imply that every reader uses Supabase. Present this integration conditionally (for example, 'If you use Supabase...') unless the user-supplied campaign context establishes it.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: The hosted platform’s paid tier does not itself raise the built-in email allowance. Moving to custom SMTP is a separate configuration decision, and Supabase still applies its own adjustable Auth rate limit afterward.
emails.mechanism: Resend provides a Supabase-specific SMTP setup path using Resend SMTP credentials. After the connection is saved, the engineer separately adjusts Supabase’s initial 30-messages-per-hour Auth limit. Resend’s own limits remain plan-specific: 100 emails per day on Free and no daily limit on Pro.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the documented Resend SMTP configuration and plan limits fit the team’s expected authentication-email volume.
emails.next_step_value: The guide provides the Supabase-specific configuration path and destination for Resend SMTP credentials; the supporting facts clarify Supabase’s separate adjustable 30-messages-per-hour starting limit and Resend’s Free and Pro allowances.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the guide does not configure the integration, raise Supabase’s Auth limit, prove production deliverability, or determine the reader’s required capacity.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: Before changing production authentication email, use Resend’s test recipient addresses to exercise delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events without affecting domain reputation.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
alternative_arguments.why_it_fails: Ordinary test sends do not provide a controlled way to trigger each delivery outcome, and using real recipients introduces unnecessary production-like risk.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Resend supplies dedicated test addresses for delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint outcomes, allowing the Dashboard, Webhooks, and API flow to be exercised without affecting domain reputation.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: evaluating another provider means risking real messages or committing to a production switch. After: the reader can first validate specific delivery-event handling in a controlled test.
must_not_say: Do not claim test addresses validate the Supabase SMTP route end to end.
Do not claim test mode predicts production deliverability or production rate-limit behavior.
Do not broaden the argument into security, integrations, templates, Automations, Broadcasts, or dedicated IPs.
alternative_arguments.objection: I do not want to risk sending real authentication messages just to evaluate another provider.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether Resend exposes the controlled delivery outcomes needed to test the application’s email-event handling.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The page identifies Resend test addresses for delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events and explains that they can be used with the Dashboard, Webhooks, and API without affecting domain reputation.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: This test does not establish that Supabase SMTP is configured correctly, that production messages will reach the inbox, or that production limits are sufficient.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame the open around testing authentication-email failure paths safely, not around a generic product announcement.

events.subject: Route Supabase Auth through Resend
events.preview_text: See the SMTP setup and the limits that apply in each system.
events.body:
Resend, an email sending platform for developers, is now available as a custom SMTP provider for Supabase Auth. If you use Supabase, you can route signup confirmations, password resets, invites, magic links, and OTPs through Resend.

The documented setup takes you from Supabase’s Authentication settings to the destination for your Resend SMTP credentials. This gives you a defined configuration path when the built-in provider’s 429 limit no longer fits your expected volume.

The limits remain separate. After custom SMTP is saved, Supabase initially applies an adjustable Auth rate limit of **30 messages per hour**. Resend Free allows 100 emails per day, while Pro has no daily sending limit.

Read the Supabase SMTP guide to inspect the configuration and decide whether those limits fit your authentication-email volume.

events.subject: Logs cannot test every outcome
events.preview_text: Simulate delivered, bounced, and complaint events before changing production email.
events.body:
If you use Supabase Auth, checking Auth logs can help investigate a 429. Those logs cannot trigger each delivery outcome your application may need to handle.

Resend is an email sending platform for developers, available as a custom SMTP provider for Supabase Auth. You can evaluate its event handling before changing production authentication email.

Dedicated test addresses simulate delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events. They work with Resend’s Dashboard, Webhooks, and API without sending real messages to real people or affecting your domain reputation.

This is a controlled test of Resend’s delivery events. It does not confirm that Supabase SMTP is configured correctly, predict production inbox placement, or establish that production limits are sufficient.

Review the test email guide to see whether these outcomes cover the application behavior you need to evaluate.
